title: Majestic Majestic!
transcript: An incredible move, King D2 is a majestic double sacrifice of the only two pieces left that [music] white has. But of course, if the knight is taken, Bishop takes D3 is just a checkmate. And if the Bishop is taken, knight to C3 is another checkmate. So black plays rook to B3, now defending both threats of checkmate at the same time. White really has to thread carefully here. There is only one move that continues the attack. Bishop to D1. Black realizes that almost every single piece in his position is completely paralyzed. He has no other choice but to move the rook. But the rook has to cover the check from the knight on C3. So the only move is rook to A3. And now it seems like black is simply out of the woods. There are no safe checks that you can give as white. This would be over for any mortal playing this position. But white plays the incredible and majestic only move. Bishop to B3. A sublime sacrifice. Understanding that of course if the Bishop takes, this is going to cut the communication of the rook with the C3 square and this would be a checkmate. C3 has to be defended so the rook has to take the Bishop. And now white only has one knight left and is down 16 points of material and still cannot give this check because that would simply be captured. But white plays the cool, calm, and collected King D1. There is literally no way of stopping the knight from coming to D2 and deliver another checkmate. All of these pieces are stuck. The rook has no way of defending that square in one move. So black will have to play a move and knight to D1 is going to be an incredible checkmate.
